key_insight: Laya-IsoToken enables clinical coding models to switch codebooks without target-labeled training notes by separating clinical evidence reading from code definitions.
clinical_relevance: The approach could reduce annotation burden and support faster transitions between diagnostic classifications, reimbursement groupers, and coding languages.
method: Train a clinical span reader once against a frozen multilingual concept space, without per-code classifier parameters.
Compile public target code descriptions into alignment operators in under three seconds.
Route unfamiliar concepts to an offline language-model verifier using a geometric residual.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 62.6% Micro-F1 on 32,804 ICD-9 discharges, a 5.4-point ICD-10 F1 gain over semantic crosswalks in zero-target-training evaluation, and 40.6% ICD-10 Micro-F1 with offline verification on 1,000 summaries.
watch_item: Performance in prospective hospital deployment remains unestablished; 0.0% invalid codes in the reported verifier evaluation does not mean all assigned codes were correct.
paper_title: Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation
